title: Data representation: 12 questions
subject: Computing
source: Written for computing/y11 lesson 28 (Pupil PDF worksheet: 12 data-representation questions)
intro: Lesson 28. Show your working. Use 1 KB = 1,024 bytes and 1 byte = 8 bits.

questions.q: Convert the binary number 10110110 to denary.
Convert the denary number 157 to 8-bit binary.
Convert the hexadecimal number 3C to denary.
Convert the binary number 11101001 to hexadecimal.
Write −45 as an 8-bit two's complement binary number.
What denary value does the two's complement number 11110110 represent?
Add the unsigned binary numbers 01101100 and 00111010.
Add the unsigned binary numbers 11001000 and 01010000. What happens?
questions.a: The result needs 9 bits (200 + 80 = 280): the 8 bits store 00011000 and the carry is lost: an overflow error

questions.q: Apply a logical shift left by 2 places to 00010110. What is the effect on its value?
Apply an arithmetic shift right by 1 place to the two's complement number 11100100. What is the effect?
questions.a: 11110010; −28 becomes −14: divided by 2, the sign bit is kept

questions.q: An image is 800 × 600 pixels with a colour depth of 24 bits. Calculate its file size in KB.
A mono sound is sampled at 44,100 Hz with a bit depth of 16 bits for 30 seconds. Calculate its size in bytes.
